title: Favorite trombone players
summary: French names Johnny Lindsey and August Russo, and George Russo and Lewis on clarinet; complaint that good clarinetists are gone.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Oh, who's your favorite trombone player through the years? Say when you first started, who
was your favorite trombone player? Johnny Lindsey, August Russo, but August Russo wasn't, you know, that's what most was read. You didn't pick up many ideas from him or
you didn't pick up many ideas. Johnny Lindsey was a good bass player too, man. He played some good bass.
George Russo, good clarinet player too, but I don't know about, you know, George Lewis. He played nice too. Mm-hm.
Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. I don't know.
Maybe that's the way I feel, you know.
You don't have a little too much of that juice in them.
You see a man like Benny Goodman, Johnny Dodge, and them fellas used to play walking planets, man.
You don't hear that no more. Saxophone. Saxophone, that's all. I find many good... Excuse me. ...clinets to play. I don't find any.
